You use if and when in the First Conditional with If clauses to exchange opinions about possible future outcomes.

You use the First Conditional to say it's possible that you will or will not do something. In that condition, something else may, may not, will or will not happen. The outcome is not in the present, but in the future.
Structure: If/When + Present Simple … will + verb …

You use when for things or events that are certain to occur.
Example: When you finish your application, you'll receive a notification. = It is certain that you will receive a notification.

You use if for things that will possibly happen.
Example: If you are the right person for the job, we will let you know. = You may be the right person for the job, but it is not certain.

Writing Tip: Should, Ought to, Had Better
You use modals like should, ought to, or had better to give strong advice, suggestions and recommendations.
The most common modals for giving advice are: should, ought to and had better.
You can think of modals as “helping verbs”. They add meaning to the main verb of a sentence. In this case, these modals add the meaning of advice.
You use these modals according to the level of suggestion you want to express.

Should is the most common modal used to give advice. You also use should for questions.
Ought to is used for giving strong advice.
Had better is much stronger than either should or ought to It is used to give an order or to suggest that something negative will happen if you refuse the advice.

Look at this job advertisement. Do you think I should apply?
If you don't apply, you will regret it. You had better brush off that resume of yours.

Bistro 88 348 Welling St. Cambridge, Massachusetts
(343) 545 4530
Hours of operation:
    Mon: 5:30 - 11:00
    Tues: 5:30 - 11:00
    Wed: 5:30 - 11:00
    Thu: 5:30 - 11:00
    Fri: 5.30 - Midnight
    Sat: 5.30 - Midnight
    Sun: 5:30 - 11:00

Description
Bistro 88, an award winning steak and seafood restaurant, is looking for strong server candidates to join our front of house team. This is a great opportunity to be a part of a fast-paced, dynamic environment. If you are looking for growth and possible management opportunities, you ought to consider Bistro as your future employer.When you look back on your decision to apply, you won't be disappointed.

Requirements/Responsibilities
Server candidates should satisfy the following criteria:
  • At least 2 years experience working in fine dining restaurants
  • A warm and outgoing personality and a passion for our industry
  • Excellent people skills and the ability to remain calm under pressure
  • A good understanding of Boston and available seafood
  • The desire and ability to work well with others
  • Extensive knowledge of and experience with computer systems
  • Provide warm, professional & knowledgeable service
  • The ability to multitask and work well in a high volume work environment
  • Must have a commitment to deliver a unique and memorable guest experience

Submit an application package which includes your Resume, Cover Letter and the creation of an online account. In your Cover Letter, please write a short paragraph describing yourself and why you would make a great addition to our team. You should include why you stand out as the ideal candidate.

Applications close November 24th.

Press the Apply button to get started now. When your online application is complete you will receive a confirmation e-mail.

Best of luck!
